dtype.summary: numpy.dtype creates a data-type object describing how NumPy array elements are represented. It supports scalar, structured, and other dtype specifications.
dtype.explanation: numpy.dtype creates a data-type object that specifies how array elements are represented and interpreted. It can describe scalar types, item size, byte order, structured fields, and sub-array shape, and NumPy accepts dtype-compatible values wherever a data type is required.

parameters.name: copy

example.title: Structured array dtype
example.code:
import numpy as np

dt = np.dtype([('id', np.int32), ('score', np.float64)])
a = np.array([(1, 9.5), (2, 8.0)], dtype=dt)

print(a.dtype)
print(a['score'])
example.explanation: Defines a structured dtype and uses it to create an array with named integer and floating-point fields.
